Add production safeguards for small .NET teams embedding AI workflows: verified deployment startup, conservative recovery after uncertain external effects, recipient-aware MCP response checks, and provider usage that preserves unknown counts.

## Changes

- Promote the verified consumer into published Infrastructure APIs and add `AddAshlarVerifiedBricks`. Host startup exposes only the pinned verified deployment set, refuses later registry overrides, and disposes owned contexts. Signer policy collections are immutable.
- Persist operation keys and intent before dispatch. Bind recovery to immutable inputs, stage configuration, and topology. Refuse unsafe retry/fallback/resume and corrupt or unbound legacy checkpoints.
- Enforce trusted caller clearance and operator response classifications on MCP tool results before and after serialization, including labelled toolbox reads and sensitive error paths.
- Capture provider-reported usage, retry attribution, missing/invalid counts, and resume lineage. Cover legacy providers and the default MEAI path without conflating logical model calls with observed HTTP attempts.
- Add an outside-checkout, package-only real certification gate-to-host smoke to the native readiness matrix. It checks exact module identity, execution after DLL replacement, and tampered startup refusal.
- Make existing timestamp and audit-file collision tests independent of local timezone and disk timing, retaining their original data-preservation assertions.

## Compatibility and limits

Unannotated pipeline stages now stop automatic replay after uncertain effects. Completed legacy checkpoints need verifiable input fingerprints. MCP responses need explicit classification and sufficient authenticated clearance; missing configuration fails closed. Migration guidance is in `docs/architecture/PipelineEffectRecovery.md` and `docs/architecture/ProtocolIntegration-MCP-A2A.md`.

Connector-side atomic deduplication remains necessary for idempotent effects. The host and its configuration remain trusted. MCP response checks do not yet cover API/gRPC/A2A/Fleet/mesh responses. Usage observations are not invoice totals or hard spending guarantees. The real-gate package smoke proves fresh .NET 10 artifacts; the same-artifact runtime matrix remains separate in #852.

## Testing

- [Hosted certification gate](https://github.com/IanFrelinger/Ashlar/actions/runs/40159555673/job/121068063234): all 3,395 tests passed. The local certification rerun passed 3,394 tests with zero skips.
- [Complete Linux coverage gate](https://github.com/IanFrelinger/Ashlar/actions/runs/40159555675/job/121068062428): Domain 98 passed / 100% lines; Infrastructure 5,474 passed, 8 skipped / 85.78% lines; Application 457 passed / 72.46% lines. All coverage floors passed.
- Clean local rebuilds passed with zero warnings/errors. Kernel host tests (46), pipeline lifecycle/validation (22), MEAI pipeline (107), MCP server (84), MCP client (40), and repaired persistence/audit-sink fixtures (15) passed. Focused production safeguard and usage suites also passed.
- Fresh local package graph and isolated NuGet-only smoke passed all 14 assertions with `ASHLAR_STRICT_MODE=1` and `ASHLAR_ALLOW_MOCK=1`. A missing-feed negative control produced its own FAIL manifest without a stale success result.
- Native [Windows](https://github.com/IanFrelinger/Ashlar/actions/runs/40159555642/job/121068154593), [Linux](https://github.com/IanFrelinger/Ashlar/actions/runs/40159555642/job/121068154469), and [macOS](https://github.com/IanFrelinger/Ashlar/actions/runs/40159555642/job/121068154464) readiness passed. Full logs verify all 14 named package-deployment assertions and zero consumer build warnings/errors on each OS.
- [Readiness summary](https://github.com/IanFrelinger/Ashlar/actions/runs/40159555642/job/121073604995) passed with `partial lanes_ran=3 lanes_skipped=1`: native platforms, Ubuntu/Alpine/Debian containers, and Docker CLI passed; the Docker API/quickstart/agent-server image lane was intentionally skipped. This is not a full all-image release verification.
- Dependency boundary, hosting package-graph alignment, workflow contexts, documentation paths, knowledge-graph freshness, PowerShell parsing, testing strategy, and diff checks passed.

Full Infrastructure coverage is measured on Linux. A local Windows full-suite attempt was stopped during slow API/CLI startup and is not counted as a complete coverage pass. Windows/macOS validation here comes from the native readiness and package-consumer checks.

## Checklist

- [x] Documentation and migration behavior updated.
- [x] Production-style tests cover changed execution boundaries.
- [x] Not a versioned release.
